thread:
lee: Taking handoff now (07:00-19:00 UTC). Quick incident context in case someone else runs into it while I'm primary.

lee: Summary: intermittent 504s against /v1/embeddings in eu-west-1 between 06:12-06:40 UTC. Root cause looks like slow kv-cache evictions causing backend timeouts; mitigations put in place and traffic healthy now.

oncall-bot: ALERT  2026-03-16T06:12:03Z  high-latency  route:/v1/embeddings  sev:p2  paged:@eng-oncall

lee: Timeline:
- 06:12 UTC: alert triggers; rate of 504s ~20-25% for embeddings within a 5m window
- 06:13 UTC: Nora (secondary) and I started mitigation runbook steps
- 06:15 UTC: increased proxy read_timeout from 10s -> 20s for eu-west proxy pool (temp)
- 06:18 UTC: kicked kv-cache rewarm jobs for top 50 tenant prefixes
- 06:22 UTC: rotated one suspicious cache node out of LB (drain + restart)
- 06:28 UTC: error-rate dropped to baseline, traffic restored

nora: Confirming — I observed long GC pauses on cache-node-7 that aligned with the timeout windows. Heap growth pattern looks abnormal; collecting heapdumps now.

lee: Actions taken (short):
- temporary timeout bump on proxy (will revert in 2h)
- cache node restart + rewarm
- created incident ticket INC-2026-099 with initial impact note
- opened engineering follow-up TKT-8001 (kv eviction tuning) and TKT-8002 (proxy timeouts audit)

hannah: FYI I ran a quick customer impact query: approx 9 premium tenants saw degraded embeddings responses (percentile-based) for ~5-8 minutes. No API key compromise.

ops-bot: Deploy note: relay-cache service rolled forward at 05:50 UTC (release relay-cache-2026.03.16-1). Marked for RCA.

lee: Runbook link I followed: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-latency. Steps used: 1 (identify), 2 (increase timeouts), 4 (cache rewarm), 6 (rotate nodes).

lee: Commands used for the cache drain:
```
kubectl cordon cache-node-7 -n prod
kubectl drain cache-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/relay-cache -n prod
```

nora: For heapdump collection I used the jcmd snippet and pushed to s3:
```
jcmd <pid> GC.heap_dump /tmp/heapdump-node7.hprof
aws s3 cp /tmp/heapdump-node7.hprof s3://redwood-debug/heapdumps/2026-03-16/node7.hprof
```

lee: Coverage note / gap: there's a 45m slot tomorrow 08:30-09:15 UTC where we only have one named oncall (me). Need a volunteer to be secondary or I'll extend. Also need someone to own the customer comms if CS asks.

diego: I can cover 08:30-09:15 UTC tomorrow, and I'll be available to field CS if needed.

lee: Thanks diego 44d marking that under TKT-8003 (handoff coverage).

hannah: Post-handoff followups I will take: assemble tenant list + performance graphs into INC-2026-099, and book a 45m postmortem sync (proposed 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC) with eng-runtime + infra.

lee: Owner matrix:
- Nora: RCA artifacts (heapdump, GC traces) -> TKT-8001 (due EOD+1)
- Diego: short CS-ready blurb + temporary coverage -> TKT-8003 (due today)
- Hannah: Impact analysis + schedule retro -> INC-2026-099 followup
- Lee (me): revert proxy timeout in 2h and validate autoscaler thresholds for cache pool -> TKT-8002

nora: Will also add a note to TKT-8001 suggesting we consider tuning the cache eviction pressure and adding alerting for >60s node-level latency.

lee: One engineering suggestion: add an automated smoke check that requests a small embedding for a pinned tenant each minute from each region; fail if 5xx rate > 1%. I'll add that to TKT-8001.

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach logs to tickets. Use /attach-logs --ticket TKT-8001 --since 06:00 --until 07:00

lee: Handing off now. Primary = lee, Secondary = nora (except tomorrow morning for 45m slot where diego will cover). Thread pinned for followups. If anything pages escalate to @pager-ops.

lee: End of handoff thread. Please update the tickets above rather than starting new threads unless urgent.
